WAF fleet view

Read-only, fleet-wide picture of every visible FortiWeb's server policies, protection profiles, protection coverage, file-backed artifacts and authored exceptions, with per-table CSV and a ZIP export.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Operations → WAF → Overview / Inventory / Profiles / Coverage / Artifacts / Exceptions (URL /waf/)

What is it?#

Operations → WAF is a set of six read-only pages that describe the WAF configuration of every FortiWeb the current console can see. They read SATOM's stored configuration snapshots, so opening them contacts no appliance, and every page states how many device/ADOM scopes it covers and how fresh their snapshots are.

What does it do?#

Page URL Answers
Overview /waf/ Headline figures, What this fleet would want fixed, six charts and a snapshot freshness table
Inventory /waf/inventory Every server policy, its enforcement, TLS, profile and signature policy
Profiles /waf/profiles Every Web Protection Profile, how many policies use it and how many of its slots are filled
Coverage /waf/coverage Protection × scope matrix
Artifacts /waf/artifacts File-backed WAF objects the estate needs, what SATOM holds, and what could not be migrated today
Exceptions /waf/exceptions Every carve-out authored in SATOM across all visible scopes, and who holds it

Each page also offers a CSV of its table and the shared Export this fleet view panel (one ZIP with CSV, Excel and PDF).

Enforcement posture. Each server policy falls into exactly one bucket, in this order: Disabled, No profile, Detection only (monitor mode on), Blocking. The overview tiles count each condition on its own, so a disabled policy that also has no profile is counted in both tiles.

Requirements#

  • At least one FortiWeb whose configuration has been harvested into the source of truth. A scope with no snapshot is shown as never harvested and contributes nothing to the figures; one older than 26 hours is marked stale.
  • The Artifacts page additionally needs an artifact sweep (see WAF Artifacts); policies never walked by a sweep appear as a number, not as zero.

Permissions#

protection.view opens every page, the CSVs and the export; without it the WAF fleet menu is hidden and the pages answer 403 Forbidden. What you see is limited to the appliances visible to you — maintenance-mode devices are hidden unless you hold appliances.view_maintenance, and the FortiWeb ADOM shows only FortiWeb devices.

The menu is live in the FortiWeb ADOM. The FortiADC ADOM draws it greyed out with the reason; the Global, FortiGate, FortiAnalyzer and FortiAuthenticator menus do not draw it (since 2026-10-14; before that the Global ADOM listed it). In the Global ADOM the pages still open from a bookmark or by URL and count every FortiWeb you may see; from the other device consoles a /waf/ URL redirects to that console's home.

How to use#

Read the fleet overview#

  1. Open Operations → WAF → Overview in the FortiWeb ADOM.
  2. Read the scope line first: Fleet-wide — N device/ADOM scopes visible here, M reporting, plus stale / never harvested badges or all snapshots fresh.
  3. Review the tiles (Server policies, Blocking (enabled, profile, not monitor-only), Monitor-mode: logs, never blocks, No web protection profile, virtual servers and pools).
  4. Under What this fleet would want fixed, each line names a count and why it matters — monitor-mode policies, policies with no profile, policies naming a profile absent from the snapshot, TLS 1.0/1.1, TLS without a certificate, disabled policies, unused custom profiles.
  5. Charts: Enforcement posture, Policies per device / ADOM, Protection coverage, Transport security, Signature policy in use and Configuration changes, last 30 days.

Filter the inventory or profiles#

  1. Open Inventory (or Profiles).
  2. Choose Device / ADOM, then Enforcement and Transport (inventory) or Origin and Usage (profiles), optionally type in Search, and click Filter.
  3. Click Download exactly these rows for a CSV of the filtered table.

Usage → Custom and unused lists custom profiles no server policy names.

Read the coverage matrix#

Each cell counts the server policies of that scope whose profile has the slot, and how many of them fill it (on/applicable). Policies with no profile are absent from every denominator. Click CSV for the matrix as a file.

Review artifacts and exceptions#

  • Artifacts: filter by Device / ADOM, Object type, State (including Needed and not held here) and Flag (Empty content, Stale reference). The tiles and charts above always show the whole visible fleet; only the table follows the filters.
  • Exceptions: filter by type, category, scope and state (active, stale, disabled, predates versioning), then Filter or Reset. CSV of these rows downloads the filtered table. The page reminds you: These are AUTHORED carve-outs, not device state.

To author or push a carve-out, use Exceptions & Signature on the device itself; the device page links back here through Fleet inventory.

Export the fleet view#

  1. Expand Export this fleet view on any page.
  2. Under Contents tick the datasets; under File formats tick CSV (one file per dataset), Excel workbook (.xlsx) and/or PDF report (with charts). All boxes start ticked.
  3. Click Download ZIP.

The bundle is always the whole visible fleet — page filters do not narrow it. The selection is in the URL, so the link can be bookmarked.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Contents (set) Datasets: Overview figures & charts, Server policies, Web protection profiles, Protection coverage, Artifacts (file-backed objects), Exceptions with their profiles At least one all
File formats (fmt) csv, xlsx, pdf At least one csv, pdf
Inventory tls filter tls (TLS terminated), weak (TLS 1.0/1.1 enabled), plain (Plain HTTP) No weak
Profiles only filter used (Bound to a policy), orphan (Custom and unused) No orphan
format=csv On any page URL, returns that page's table as CSV No /waf/inventory?format=csv

Example#

🧪Example — Find policies that never block

A security lead opens Operations → WAF → Inventory, sets Enforcement to Detection only and clicks Filter. The table lists every policy running in monitor mode on fweb-01 and fweb-02, and Download exactly these rows gives the list for the change review.

Result#

  • Pages and CSVs change nothing.
  • Download ZIP returns satom-waf-fleet-<date>-<time>.zip with a MANIFEST.txt (who, when, scopes covered and which reported), a csv/ folder (always including scopes.csv), the workbook and/or the PDF. The download is recorded in the audit log as waf.export.

Troubleshooting#

"select at least one dataset to export" / "select at least one file format"#

Possible causes — every box in one of the two groups was unticked.

Solution — the message is shown on the page you exported from (including Exceptions). Tick at least one dataset and one format, then Download ZIP again.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: an empty export started from the Exceptions page now returns to that page instead of the Overview.

Verification — the browser downloads a ZIP file.

A scope shows "never harvested"#

Possible causes - The device has never been synced into the source of truth.

Solution — run a device sync for it (see Jobs and Scheduled actions), then reload the page.

Verification — the scope counts as reporting in the scope line.

Numbers look out of date#

Possible causes — the pages show configuration as of the last harvest, not live state; a stale badge means the newest snapshot is older than 26 hours.

Solution — refresh the device configuration, then reload.

The Excel workbook is missing from the ZIP#

Possible causes — the dataset is too large for the workbook writer.

Solution — read MANIFEST.txt: it carries an Excel workbook OMITTED: … note; use the CSV files instead.

Advanced Internals
  • All six pages narrow the device list once through the visible-appliance filter and compute every figure from that one result.
  • The charts load their data from /waf/api/summary.json, /waf/api/artifacts.json and /waf/api/exceptions.json (protection.view required). The PDF in the export re-renders the same series server-side.
  • PDF tables are cut at 40 rows; the CSV and workbook in the same ZIP carry the full data.
  • The Exceptions dataset is desired state: SATOM does not record whether a carve-out was ever pushed to a device, so no row claims it was.
